source.title: How You Start Matters for Generalization
source.authors: Sameera Ramasinghe; L. MacDonald; M. Farazi; Hemanth Saratchandran; Simon Lucey

record.file_problem: none; full paper text including appendix is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests whether initialization changes generalization using a different intervention: it trains deep classifiers on random labels, then trains them on natural labels and compares their test accuracy with models using random initialization.
record.gate_note: Experiment 4 and Appendix Table 3 report natural-label train/test accuracy after random initialization versus random-label pre-training. The random-label pre-training step is an initialization intervention; random-label fit itself is not the natural-label generalization outcome. Other regression and spectral-bias experiments concern smooth interpolation or frequency dynamics, not the listed versions. Hessian results concern flatness and are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: Random-label training supplies an initialization intervention; the reported outcomes compare subsequent natural-label training under two initializations. The study does not report random-label training and held-out accuracies needed to test V1's coexistence claim. Its other experiments measure spectral dynamics, interpolation smoothness, or unnormalized Hessian geometry rather than the remaining versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that initialization spectrum substantially affects generalization and that the association between flatness and generalization depends on architecture. Appendix A.3 further shows that low initial bandwidth alone does not ensure smooth interpolation; frequency convergence-decay rates also matter.
record.recipe_differences: Uses random-label pre-training as a high-bandwidth initialization and compares it with random weights before natural-label training; the study does not reproduce the claim versions' interventions. It also omits data augmentation in the classification experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization bandwidth and network architecture; the reported test-accuracy drop under high-bandwidth initialization occurs across tested models and datasets, with the size of the change varying by model and dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: Across all 30 classification settings, random-label pre-training lowers subsequent natural-label test accuracy despite 100% natural-label training accuracy in both initialization conditions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested classifiers without data augmentation, random-label pre-training produces an initialization from which subsequent natural-label training generalizes worse than training from random initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: In regression, Gaussian networks with nonsmooth interpolations have lower Hessian trace and spectral norm than those with smooth interpolations; ReLU networks show the opposite ordering.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The association between unnormalized Hessian flatness and interpolation smoothness depends on activation and initialization in these regression experiments.

record.problems: The classification experiments omit data augmentation, which the authors treat as explicit regularization. ImageNet uses only three models because of resource use. ImageNet table values have no uncertainty reported. The paper states that reproducing materials were not included and does not report compute resources.
record.rows_left_out: None; all separately reported natural-label train/test results from Sections 7 and Appendix A.2 are included. The random-label pre-training accuracy results are not natural-label generalization outcomes and were not recorded as rows.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fixed-random-label fitting together with chance random-label held-out accuracy and above-chance natural-label accuracy under the same training recipe. Random-label pre-training accuracies are not reported; dropout and batch normalization are retained.
Width increases beyond the width required for zero training error and their effect on held-out error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under specified tuning budgets or recovery interventions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout, including interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.

Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance and its ranking of classification generalization gaps against norm- and margin-based measures. Hessian trace, spectral norm, and regression smoothness do not measure this version.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equal numbers of random examples.

record.verdict_notes: All recorded numerical values match Tables 1 and 3. Their training accuracies concern the final natural-label stage, not random-label pre-training. Table 1 uncertainties are standard deviations across five runs. The initialization penalty does not challenge V1: even the poorer natural-label test accuracies remain far above chance. The Hessian counterexamples do not challenge V7's magnitude-aware measure.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting fixed random labels with natural-label generalization under the same recipe as Zhang et al.; random labels are used only to pre-train before natural-label training.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold comparison.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measure or comparison of gap-ranking measures.

rows.subject: VGG11
rows.stage_stated: trained on CIFAR10 train split with correct labels after either random initialization or pre-training on randomly shuffled labels
rows.operation_detail: Compared natural-label training from random weights with natural-label training starting from weights pre-trained on randomly shuffled labels.
rows.baseline: High B/W initialization: 100% train accuracy; 71.94 ± 0.71% test accuracy
rows.note: This natural-label outcome follows the random-initialization condition; the paper does not compare its results with the specific behavior asserted by any listed version.
